user.title: Smart Thermostat — Choose mode
user.description: Choose how you want to configure the thermostat. You can change the mode at any time from options.

data_description.config_mode:
🟢 SIMPLE — Just a few essential fields. Set the AC, the desired temperature for day and night, and which alerts to receive. The system handles everything automatically. Ideal for those who want simplicity without giving up intelligent temperature control.

🔵 SIMPLE WITH SOLAR — Like Simple, but adds solar management: the AC turns on when you are producing enough solar energy and turns off when production drops.

⚙️ FULL — Access to all advanced parameters: thermal profiles, sensor calibration, presence boost, separate quiet hours for Google and Telegram, notification limits, and much more. For those who want maximum control over the thermostat behaviour.

profilo.title: Regulation profile
profilo.description: Choose how the thermostat should behave. The profile determines how quickly the system cools and how sensitive it is to temperature changes.

data_description.profile:
🔵 BALANCED (recommended) — Turns on at +1.5°C above target, high fan from +2.0°C. Gradual cooling for everyday use.

🔴 AGGRESSIVE — Turns on at +1.2°C, high fan from +1.6°C. Cools faster, ideal for large or sun-exposed rooms.

🟢 GENTLE — Turns on at +1.8°C, high fan from +2.4°C. Quiet and discreet, perfect for sleeping.

⚙️ CUSTOM — Set every threshold manually in the next step.

soglie_termiche.title: Custom thermal thresholds
soglie_termiche.description: These parameters precisely control how the thermostat reacts to temperature. Only visible with the Custom profile.

data.below_offset: Margin below target to slow down (°C)
data.turn_on_offset: Minimum offset to turn on from solar (°C)
data.extreme_delta: Setpoint delta in extreme heat band (°C)
data.manual_shutoff_timer_enabled: Enable automatic shutoff if turned on manually?

data_description.extreme_offset: Above target + this: max fan and very low setpoint. Example: 2.0°C → extreme heat above 27°C.
data_description.hot_offset: Above target + this: medium fan and low setpoint. Example: 1.5°C → strong heat between 26.5 and 27°C.
data_description.range_offset: Above target + this: low fan and slightly reduced setpoint. Example: 0.2°C → mild heat between 25.2 and 26.5°C.
data_description.below_offset: Below target - this: AC slows down to avoid over-cooling. Example: 0.1°C → slows below 24.9°C.
data_description.turn_on_offset: Turns on from solar only if room > target + this. Example: 1.5°C → only above 26.5°C.
data_description.temp_delta: How much the setpoint is lowered in normal bands. Example: 1.0°C → sends 24°C with target 25°C.
data_description.extreme_delta: How much the setpoint is lowered in extreme heat. Example: 2.0°C → sends 23°C in extreme heat.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_min: If enabled from the card, after a manual accension the AC turns off automatically after this many minutes, regardless of the master switch — useful for fully manual use (e.g. a portable heater). Set to 0 to never offer this feature in the card.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_enabled: If enabled, the shutoff timer (set below) starts automatically on every manual accension, without needing to activate it each time from the card — you can still enable/disable it anytime from the card. Always applies, even if the automation master switch is disabled.

energia.description: Configure how the thermostat uses solar production to automatically control the AC. Leave sensors empty to completely disable this feature.

data.soc_min: Minimum battery charge to turn on (%)

data.fv_shutoff_manual: Turn off even if manually turned on

data_description.fv_sensor: Watts produced by panels in real time. Example: sensor.solar_panels_total.
data_description.fv_margin_w: Surplus required above consumption to turn on. Example: 1200W → turns on only if producing 1200W more than consuming.
data_description.soc_min: Minimum battery charge required to enable turn-on. Example: 70 → turns on only with battery ≥ 70%.
data_description.fv_start_time: Does not turn on automatically before this time. Example: 10:00.
data_description.fv_end_time: Does not turn on automatically after this time. Example: 16:00.
data_description.fv_priority: With multiple thermostats, lower number turns on first and off last. Example: bedroom=10, living=20.
data_description.fv_stagger_minutes: Pause between successive turn-ons to avoid consumption peaks. Example: 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: turns off the AC when solar surplus stays below threshold for N consecutive samples. With multiple thermostats, turns off the highest priority number first.
data_description.fv_shutoff_delay_min: How many consecutive samples (one per general update cycle) of insufficient surplus must accumulate before turning off. Example: 5 samples with a 5-minute update cycle = 25 confirmed minutes. The window is sliding: one high value does not reset the buffer, it just shifts it.
data_description.fv_shutoff_threshold: The surplus (production - consumption) must be below this value in ALL the last N samples to trigger turn-off. Value 0 = turns off when solar no longer covers consumption. Positive value = turns off earlier, when surplus drops below X Watts. Example: 500W → turns off when surplus is below 500W for N consecutive samples.
data_description.fv_shutoff_extra_hours: Extra hours after window end when it can still turn off. Example: window ends at 16:00, extra 1h → can turn off until 17:00.
data_description.fv_shutoff_manual: If enabled, the FV-drop shutoff also applies to a manually turned-on AC, not only to those turned on automatically by solar.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off: If enabled, after a manual shutoff the thermostat avoids automatically turning the AC back on for the number of hours configured below.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off_hours: For how many hours, after a manual shutoff, the thermostat avoids automatically turning the AC back on.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_enabled: If enabled, an AC turned on by solar automatically turns off when the FV production sensor stops responding for too long — without that data we can no longer know if there's actually sunlight. Applies ONLY to AC units turned on by solar: a manual accension is never affected. Has no effect at night, since night accension never goes through the solar check.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_min: After how many minutes of FV sensor offline this specific AC turns off. An alert notification is sent anyway within a few minutes of detection, regardless of this value.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_tts: Voice alert (Google Home) when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_telegram: Telegram alert when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.

modalita_notturna.title: Night mode

data.night_end_shutoff_auto_only: ▶ Turn off at end of night only if turned on automatically
data.presence_boost_enabled: ▶ Fan boost if presence detected and still warm

data.presence_boost_offset: Degrees above target to trigger boost (°C)
data.window_delay_minutes: Minutes with window open before turning off AC

data_description.night_start_time: Night mode starts at this time. The window can span midnight. Example: 23:00.
data_description.night_end_time: Night mode ends at this time. Example: 07:00.
data_description.night_offset: At night the effective target becomes target + this value. Example: target 25°C + 1°C = night target 26°C. Set 0 to keep the same target.
data_description.night_ac_enabled: If enabled: turns on the AC at night if the room exceeds night target + threshold, without needing solar.
data_description.night_turn_on_offset: How much the room must exceed the night target to trigger automatic turn-on. Example: night target 26°C + 1.5°C → turns on above 27.5°C.
data_description.night_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: turns off the AC when the room stays at temperature for the configured minutes. Works regardless of how it was turned on.
data_description.night_shutoff_delta: Tolerance above night target. Example: target 26°C, delta 0.3°C → 'at temperature' when ≤ 26.3°C. If it rises above, countdown restarts.
data_description.night_shutoff_min: Consecutive minutes at temperature before turning off. Example: 30 minutes.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: when night mode ends (e.g. at 07:00), the AC is turned off ALWAYS, regardless of why it was on — manual, solar, or automatic night turn-on. Useful to avoid leaving the AC running all morning.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_auto_only: If enabled: when night mode ends, the AC is turned off ONLY IF it was turned on automatically by night mode. If you turned it on manually or via solar, nothing happens. Can be enabled together with 'always' — in that case 'always' takes precedence.
data_description.presence_boost_enabled: If enabled: raises fan to medium when presence is detected continuously and the room is still warm.
data_description.presence_boost_minutes: Minutes of continuous presence before boost activates. Example: 10 minutes.
data_description.presence_boost_offset: Boost only if room > target + this. Example: 1°C → boost only above 26°C with target 25°C.
data_description.window_delay_minutes: Minutes to wait before turning off due to open window. Example: 5 minutes → alerts immediately, turns off after 5 minutes.
data_description.update_interval_minutes: How often the thermostat checks and updates. Example: 5 minutes.
data_description.calibration_max_offset: Maximum correction for difference between room sensor and AC internal sensor. Example: 3°C.
data_description.min_below_internal: The setpoint always stays at least this value below the AC internal sensor. Example: 1°C → if AC reads 24°C internally, setpoint never exceeds 23°C.

data_description.notify_targets: HA notify entities for Telegram. Example: notify.telegram_user.
data_description.notify_chat_ids: Telegram chat IDs separated by comma. Only if you have no notify entities.
data_description.notify_temp_change_enabled: If enabled: Telegram on every setpoint change. Can be frequent.
data_description.notify_temp_change_limit_enabled: If enabled: setpoint change Telegram notifications are sent at most once every X minutes. Useful to reduce messages when the thermostat frequently adjusts the setpoint. Quiet hours always take precedence and block notifications regardless of this setting.
data_description.notify_temp_change_limit_min: How many minutes must pass between setpoint change notifications. Example: 30 minutes → even if the setpoint changes every 5 minutes, a notification arrives at most every 30 minutes.
data_description.notify_temp_change_message: Variables: {{ name }}, {{ old_temp }}, {{ new_temp }}, {{ fan_mode }}, {{ room_temp }}, {{ target }}.
data_description.notify_power_tts: If enabled: Google Home announces when the AC turns on/off automatically due to solar or night mode, explaining the reason.
data_description.notify_power_notify: If enabled: Telegram when AC turns on/off automatically due to solar or night mode. Enabled by default.
data_description.notify_night_end_tts: If enabled: Google Home announces when the AC is turned off at the end of night mode. Separate channel from other alerts — you can keep this on even if others are silenced.
data_description.notify_night_end_notify: If enabled: Telegram receives a message when the AC turns off at the end of night mode. Separate channel. Enabled by default so you always know when the AC switches off in the morning.
data_description.door_alert_enabled: If enabled: alerts on both door opening and closing. Informational only, never acts on the AC.
data_description.door_alert_tts: Door alert via Google Home. Requires 'Door alert' enabled.
data_description.door_alert_notify: Door alert via Telegram. Requires 'Door alert' enabled.
data_description.quiet_enabled: If enabled: during the configured time window, some alerts are silenced according to preferences below.
data_description.quiet_start_time: Quiet period starts at this time. Can span midnight. Example: 23:00.
data_description.quiet_end_time: Quiet period ends at this time. Example: 07:00.
data_description.quiet_tts: If enabled: Google Home does not speak during quiet hours for automatic turn-on/off alerts.
data_description.quiet_notify: If enabled: Telegram suspends automatic turn-on/off messages during quiet hours.

data_description.name: The name this thermostat will appear as in Home Assistant. Example: 'Bedroom'.
data_description.climate_entity: The physical AC to control. Example: climate.ac_bedroom.
data_description.temp_sensor: External room temperature sensor (e.g. Zigbee probe). If left empty, the thermostat uses the AC's internal sensor. ⚠️ The AC internal sensor reads only integer values (e.g. 25°C, not 25.3°C) so turn-on and turn-off thresholds adapt automatically. Example: sensor.temperature_bedroom. Leave empty to use the AC internal sensor.
data_description.simple_external_sensor_stale_min: If the external sensor (e.g. an MQTT sensor depending on a remote server) stops updating for more than this many minutes, the thermostat automatically switches to the AC's internal sensor, to avoid regulating based on stale data. It switches back on its own as soon as the external sensor resumes updating. Default 45 minutes.
data_description.window_sensor: Binary sensor 'on' when window is open. If set: alerts on opening and turns off AC after 5 minutes if still open, then turns it back on when closed. Leave empty to disable.
data_description.door_sensor: Binary sensor 'on' when door is open. If set: sends an alert when door opens or closes. Never acts on AC. Leave empty to disable.
data_description.window_detection_enabled: If disabled, the window has no effect on the AC at all — no shutoff when it opens, no alert when manually turning on with the window already open. Useful if the sensor is unreliable in certain conditions (e.g. doesn't update correctly during prolonged kitchen use).

simple_temperature.title: Thermostat — Temperatures and schedules
simple_temperature.description: Set the desired temperature for daytime and nighttime, with their respective schedules.

data.night_end_shutoff_enabled: ▶ Turn off AC at the end of night mode (always)
data.night_end_shutoff_auto_only: ▶ Turn off at end of night only if turned on automatically
data.simple_turn_on_offset: Minimum offset above target to turn on (°C)
data.simple_shutoff_margin: Margin below target before turning off (°C)
data.simple_no_auto_on_night: ▶ Do not turn on AC automatically at night
data.simple_dry_max_min: Maximum time in dehumidification before switching to cooling (min)
data.manual_shutoff_timer_enabled: Enable automatic shutoff if turned on manually?

data_description.simple_target_day: The temperature you want to maintain during the day. Example: 25°C → with external sensor AC starts above 26.5°C, with internal sensor above 27°C.
data_description.simple_target_night: Desired temperature at night. Usually a couple of degrees higher than daytime to avoid over-cooling. Example: 26°C.
data_description.simple_night_start: Night mode starts at this time with the nighttime target. Daytime mode starts automatically when night ends. Example: 23:00.
data_description.simple_night_end: Night mode ends at this time and daytime mode starts automatically. Example: 07:00.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: when night mode ends (e.g. at 07:00), the AC is turned off ALWAYS, regardless of why it was on.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_auto_only: If enabled: turns off at end of night ONLY IF the AC was turned on automatically. If you turned it on manually, nothing happens.
data_description.simple_turn_on_offset: How many degrees the temperature must exceed the target before the AC turns on. With external sensor the default is 0.8°C (e.g. target 25°C → turns on from 25.8°C). With internal sensor the default is 1.0°C (e.g. target 25°C → turns on from 26°C). Lower values = turns on sooner but with more cycles. Higher values = turns on only when it is really hot. Note: at the end of night mode there is always a 1-hour pause before the thermostat starts turning on the AC again, to avoid unwanted turn-ons caused by the target change.
data_description.simple_shutoff_margin: How many degrees the temperature must drop below the target before the thermostat turns off the AC. With external sensor (decimal) the margin is applied exactly as set. With internal sensor (integers only) the value is rounded using the same rule already used for temperature commands: 0.5°C or less becomes 0 (no effect, turns off as soon as target is reached), above 0.5°C becomes 1 whole degree. A higher margin keeps the room closer to target for longer, at the cost of a few extra minutes of runtime. Default 0.2°C.
data_description.simple_no_auto_on_night: If enabled: during night mode the thermostat never turns on the AC automatically, even if the temperature exceeds the configured threshold. If the AC was already on (e.g. you turned it on manually or it was left on from the afternoon), it continues to regulate and turn it off when the target temperature is reached or at end of night. Useful if you prefer to sleep without AC even on hot nights and want to control it manually.
data_description.simple_dry_enabled: If enabled: when the temperature rises slightly above the target, the AC starts in dehumidifier mode (DRY) instead of full cooling. This lowers humidity and makes the room feel fresher while using less power. After the configured maximum time (or if temperature rises further) it automatically switches to full cooling. Particularly useful in humid climates, especially during morning hours. If the temperature at start is already too high, it starts directly in cooling mode without going through dry.
data_description.simple_dry_max_min: How long the AC stays in dehumidification mode before switching to cooling. If during this time the room cools down enough, it turns off without switching to cooling. If the temperature stays high or rises, after this time it automatically switches to cooling. Example: 30 minutes → gives the dehumidifier half an hour to lower humidity, then cools if needed. Lower values (10-15 min) = less dehumidification. Higher values (45-60 min) = more dehumidification, useful in very humid mornings.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_min: If enabled from the card, after a manual accension the AC turns off automatically after this many minutes, regardless of the master switch — useful for fully manual use (e.g. a portable heater). Set to 0 to never offer this feature in the card.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_enabled: If enabled, the shutoff timer (set below) starts automatically on every manual accension, without needing to activate it each time from the card — you can still enable/disable it anytime from the card. Always applies, even if the automation master switch is disabled.
data_description.season_mode: Summer: cooling only (existing behavior). Winter: heating only. Auto: manages both, switching based on temperature, with a minimum time between switches to avoid rapid cycling in mid-season. Manual: no automation — only the shutoff timer and safety protections (e.g. open window) stay active — the master switch is automatically disabled. Off: everything off, including the timer — zero interference, fully manual control via the original remote.
data_description.simple_eco_day_enabled: Instead of turning off the air conditioner when the temperature drops below target minus the margin, switches it to Eco mode and passively follows its own internal sensor reading, without pushing further. Stays in Eco until the room temperature rises back above target plus the margin, then resumes normally recalculating the correct band. Applies only during the day — see the separate field for night. Requires the air conditioner to support an "eco" preset (check the entity's attributes in Home Assistant).
data_description.simple_eco_night_enabled: Same behavior as "Eco mode instead of shutoff (day)", but applied during the night period.

data.fv_turn_on_total_minutes: Total minutes of FV surplus before turning on

data.fv_sensor_offline_notify_tts: Voice alert for FV sensor offline
data.fv_sensor_offline_notify_telegram: Telegram alert for FV sensor offline
data.simple_sunset_anticipate_h: Hours before sunset to stop automatic control
data.fv_shutoff_manual: Turn off even if manually turned on
data.fv_shutoff_manual_delay_min: Delay before turning off a manual accension
data.simple_no_reon_manual_off: Do not turn on if manually turned off

data_description.fv_sensor: Watts produced by panels in real time. Example: sensor.solar_panels_total.
data_description.fv_margin_w: Surplus required above consumption to turn on. Example: 1200W → turns on only if producing 1200W more than consuming.
data_description.soc_min: Minimum battery charge to enable turn-on. Example: 70 → turns on only with battery ≥ 70%.
data_description.fv_priority: With multiple ACs, lower number turns on first and off last. Example: bedroom=10, living=20.
data_description.fv_stagger_minutes: Pause between successive turn-ons to avoid peaks. Example: 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: turns off when surplus stays below threshold for N consecutive samples.
data_description.fv_shutoff_total_minutes: For how many consecutive minutes the solar surplus must remain insufficient before the thermostat turns off the AC. The check always uses 4 fixed samples: the interval between samples is calculated automatically by dividing this value by 4 (example: 20 minutes → a check every 5 minutes; 12 minutes → a check every 3 minutes). A lower value makes shutoff more responsive; a higher value better protects against temporary consumption spikes (e.g. stove use). Minimum 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_turn_on_total_minutes: For how many consecutive minutes the solar surplus must remain sufficient before the thermostat turns on (or turns back on) the AC. Without this wait, turning off for insufficient FV reduces the house's consumption, which can make the surplus suddenly appear sufficient on the next cycle, causing an almost immediate restart right after shutoff. A higher value better protects against these oscillations; a lower value makes turn-on more responsive to a genuine improvement in production. Minimum 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_enabled: If enabled, an AC turned on by solar automatically turns off when the FV production sensor stops responding for too long — without that data we can no longer know if there's actually sunlight. Applies ONLY to AC units turned on by solar: a manual accension is never affected. Has no effect at night, since night accension never goes through the solar check.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_min: After how many minutes of FV sensor offline this specific AC turns off. An alert notification is sent anyway within a few minutes of detection, regardless of this value.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_tts: Voice alert (Google Home) when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_telegram: Telegram alert when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.
data_description.fv_shutoff_threshold: Surplus must stay below this for all N samples. Value 0 = turns off when FV < consumption. Example: 500W.
data_description.sunset_info: Time the sun sets today at your location, calculated automatically by Home Assistant. Updates every time you open these settings.
data_description.cutoff_info: Automatically calculated: sunset minus the configured hours. After this time the automation stops controlling the AC turned on manually and stops automatic solar turn-ons. Updates every time you open these settings.
data_description.simple_sunset_anticipate_h: How many hours before sunset the automation stops intervening. Automatic solar turn-on is active from end of night mode until this time — calculated automatically every day based on the season. Minimum 2 hours. Example: sunset 19:40 with 2 hours → automation active until 17:40.
data_description.fv_shutoff_manual: If enabled, the thermostat will turn off the AC even when it was manually turned on by the user and solar production is insufficient.
data_description.fv_shutoff_manual_delay_min: How many minutes to wait, after detecting insufficient solar surplus, before turning off an AC that was manually turned on — someone who turns it on manually is probably feeling hot and doesn't care much about solar in the short term. Minimum 10 minutes, at least 30 recommended. Does not apply to accensions triggered by solar surplus itself, which remain immediate.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off: If enabled: when you turn off the AC manually (remote, Gree app, or anything other than the thermostat), the integration will not automatically turn it back on for the number of hours configured below — this applies to normal temperature-based turn-ons as well as solar-surplus turn-ons, both during the day and at night. Once the configured hours have passed, normal behavior resumes. Useful if you want to keep it off manually without the thermostat turning it back on right away.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off_hours: How many hours, after a manual shutoff, the integration should refrain from automatically turning the AC back on. Applies both during the day and at night. Example: 2 hours → if you turn it off at 3:00 PM, the thermostat won't turn it back on before 5:00 PM, even if the temperature exceeds the threshold or solar surplus is available.

data_description.simple_target_day: The temperature you want to maintain during the day. Example: 25°C → with external sensor AC starts above 26.5°C, with internal sensor above 27°C.
data_description.simple_target_night: Desired temperature at night. Usually a couple of degrees higher than daytime to avoid over-cooling. Example: 26°C.
data_description.simple_night_start: Night mode starts at this time with the nighttime target. Daytime mode starts automatically when night ends. Example: 23:00.
data_description.simple_night_end: Night mode ends at this time and daytime mode starts automatically. Example: 07:00.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: when night mode ends (e.g. at 07:00), the AC is turned off ALWAYS, regardless of why it was on.
data_description.night_end_shutoff_auto_only: If enabled: turns off at end of night ONLY IF the AC was turned on automatically. If you turned it on manually, nothing happens.
data_description.simple_turn_on_offset: How many degrees the temperature must exceed the target before the AC turns on. With external sensor the default is 0.8°C (e.g. target 25°C → turns on from 25.8°C). With internal sensor the default is 1.0°C (e.g. target 25°C → turns on from 26°C). Lower values = turns on sooner but with more cycles. Higher values = turns on only when it is really hot. Note: at the end of night mode there is always a 1-hour pause before the thermostat starts turning on the AC again, to avoid unwanted turn-ons caused by the target change.
data_description.simple_shutoff_margin: How many degrees the temperature must drop below the target before the thermostat turns off the AC. With external sensor (decimal) the margin is applied exactly as set. With internal sensor (integers only) the value is rounded using the same rule already used for temperature commands: 0.5°C or less becomes 0 (no effect, turns off as soon as target is reached), above 0.5°C becomes 1 whole degree. A higher margin keeps the room closer to target for longer, at the cost of a few extra minutes of runtime. Default 0.2°C.
data_description.simple_no_auto_on_night: If enabled: during night mode the thermostat never turns on the AC automatically, even if the temperature exceeds the configured threshold. If the AC was already on (e.g. you turned it on manually or it was left on from the afternoon), it continues to regulate and turn it off when the target temperature is reached or at end of night. Useful if you prefer to sleep without AC even on hot nights and want to control it manually.
data_description.simple_dry_enabled: If enabled: when the temperature rises slightly above the target, the AC starts in dehumidifier mode (DRY) instead of full cooling. This lowers humidity and makes the room feel fresher while using less power. After the configured maximum time (or if temperature rises further) it automatically switches to full cooling. Particularly useful in humid climates, especially during morning hours. If the temperature at start is already too high, it starts directly in cooling mode without going through dry.
data_description.simple_dry_max_min: How long the AC stays in dehumidification mode before switching to cooling. If during this time the room cools down enough, it turns off without switching to cooling. If the temperature stays high or rises, after this time it automatically switches to cooling. Example: 30 minutes → gives the dehumidifier half an hour to lower humidity, then cools if needed. Lower values (10-15 min) = less dehumidification. Higher values (45-60 min) = more dehumidification, useful in very humid mornings.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_min: If enabled from the card, after a manual accension the AC turns off automatically after this many minutes, regardless of the master switch — useful for fully manual use (e.g. a portable heater). Set to 0 to never offer this feature in the card.
data_description.manual_shutoff_timer_enabled: If enabled, the shutoff timer (set below) starts automatically on every manual accension, without needing to activate it each time from the card — you can still enable/disable it anytime from the card. Always applies, even if the automation master switch is disabled.
data_description.season_mode: Summer: cooling only (existing behavior). Winter: heating only. Auto: manages both, switching based on temperature, with a minimum time between switches to avoid rapid cycling in mid-season. Manual: no automation — only the shutoff timer and safety protections (e.g. open window) stay active — the master switch is automatically disabled. Off: everything off, including the timer — zero interference, fully manual control via the original remote.
data_description.simple_eco_day_enabled: Instead of turning off the air conditioner when the temperature drops below target minus the margin, switches it to Eco mode and passively follows its own internal sensor reading, without pushing further. Stays in Eco until the room temperature rises back above target plus the margin, then resumes normally recalculating the correct band. Applies only during the day — see the separate field for night. Requires the air conditioner to support an "eco" preset (check the entity's attributes in Home Assistant).
data_description.simple_eco_night_enabled: Same behavior as "Eco mode instead of shutoff (day)", but applied during the night period.

energia_simple.description: Configure solar sensors. The AC will turn on automatically when you are producing enough solar energy and turn off when production drops.

data.soc_min: Minimum battery charge to turn on (%)
data.fv_shutoff_total_minutes: Total minutes of FV drop before turning off
data.fv_turn_on_total_minutes: Total minutes of FV surplus before turning on
data.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_enabled: Turn off if FV sensor is offline

data.fv_sensor_offline_notify_tts: Voice alert for FV sensor offline

data.simple_no_reon_manual_off: Do not turn on if manually turned off
data.simple_no_reon_manual_off_hours: Hours to block re-activation after manual shutoff

data_description.fv_sensor: Watts produced by panels in real time. Example: sensor.solar_panels_total.
data_description.fv_margin_w: Surplus required above consumption to turn on. Example: 1200W → turns on only if producing 1200W more than consuming.
data_description.soc_min: Minimum battery charge to enable turn-on. Example: 70 → turns on only with battery ≥ 70%.
data_description.fv_priority: With multiple ACs, lower number turns on first and off last. Example: bedroom=10, living=20.
data_description.fv_stagger_minutes: Pause between successive turn-ons to avoid peaks. Example: 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_shutoff_enabled: If enabled: turns off when surplus stays below threshold for N consecutive samples.
data_description.fv_shutoff_total_minutes: For how many consecutive minutes the solar surplus must remain insufficient before the thermostat turns off the AC. The check always uses 4 fixed samples: the interval between samples is calculated automatically by dividing this value by 4 (example: 20 minutes → a check every 5 minutes; 12 minutes → a check every 3 minutes). A lower value makes shutoff more responsive; a higher value better protects against temporary consumption spikes (e.g. stove use). Minimum 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_turn_on_total_minutes: For how many consecutive minutes the solar surplus must remain sufficient before the thermostat turns on (or turns back on) the AC. Without this wait, turning off for insufficient FV reduces the house's consumption, which can make the surplus suddenly appear sufficient on the next cycle, causing an almost immediate restart right after shutoff. A higher value better protects against these oscillations; a lower value makes turn-on more responsive to a genuine improvement in production. Minimum 5 minutes.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_enabled: If enabled, an AC turned on by solar automatically turns off when the FV production sensor stops responding for too long — without that data we can no longer know if there's actually sunlight. Applies ONLY to AC units turned on by solar: a manual accension is never affected. Has no effect at night, since night accension never goes through the solar check.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_shutoff_min: After how many minutes of FV sensor offline this specific AC turns off. An alert notification is sent anyway within a few minutes of detection, regardless of this value.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_tts: Voice alert (Google Home) when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.
data_description.fv_sensor_offline_notify_telegram: Telegram alert when the FV sensor goes offline and when this AC is turned off as a result.
data_description.fv_shutoff_threshold: Surplus must stay below this for all N samples. Value 0 = turns off when FV < consumption. Example: 500W.
data_description.sunset_info: Time the sun sets today at your location, calculated automatically by Home Assistant. Updates every time you open these settings.
data_description.cutoff_info: Automatically calculated: sunset minus the configured hours. After this time the automation stops controlling the AC turned on manually and stops automatic solar turn-ons. Updates every time you open these settings.
data_description.simple_sunset_anticipate_h: How many hours before sunset the automation stops intervening. Automatic solar turn-on is active from end of night mode until this time — calculated automatically every day based on the season. Minimum 2 hours. Example: sunset 19:40 with 2 hours → automation active until 17:40.
data_description.fv_shutoff_manual: If enabled, the thermostat will turn off the AC even when it was manually turned on by the user and solar production is insufficient.
data_description.fv_shutoff_manual_delay_min: How many minutes to wait, after detecting insufficient solar surplus, before turning off an AC that was manually turned on — someone who turns it on manually is probably feeling hot and doesn't care much about solar in the short term. Minimum 10 minutes, at least 30 recommended. Does not apply to accensions triggered by solar surplus itself, which remain immediate.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off: If enabled: when you turn off the AC manually (remote, Gree app, or anything other than the thermostat), the integration will not automatically turn it back on for the number of hours configured below — this applies to normal temperature-based turn-ons as well as solar-surplus turn-ons, both during the day and at night. Once the configured hours have passed, normal behavior resumes. Useful if you want to keep it off manually without the thermostat turning it back on right away.
data_description.simple_no_reon_manual_off_hours: How many hours, after a manual shutoff, the integration should refrain from automatically turning the AC back on. Applies both during the day and at night. Example: 2 hours → if you turn it off at 3:00 PM, the thermostat won't turn it back on before 5:00 PM, even if the temperature exceeds the threshold or solar surplus is available.

protezione_potenza.title: Power protection — Prevent circuit breaker trip
protezione_potenza.description: Configure automatic protection against circuit breaker trips. If consumption exceeds the set threshold, the AC turns off automatically and turns back on when consumption drops.

data.power_limit_hysteresis_w: Consumption reduction required to turn back on (W)
data.power_limit_restore_min: Minutes of low consumption before turning back on

data_description.power_limit_enabled: If enabled: the thermostat monitors consumption and automatically turns off the AC if it exceeds the threshold for at least 30 seconds (anti-spike). It turns back on when consumption drops enough.
data_description.power_limit_sensor: Sensor measuring the electrical consumption of the circuit to protect. Can be total house consumption or a single circuit meter. Example: sensor.living_room_consumption.
data_description.power_limit_mode: Single AC: manages only this AC independently. Multiple AC: coordinates shutdown and restart in cascade with other thermostats that have the same protection active, using the already configured priority.
data_description.power_limit_max_w: If consumption exceeds this value for at least 30 seconds, the AC turns off. The 30 seconds prevent shutdowns due to momentary spikes (e.g. washing machine start, induction hob). Example: 3500W → turns off if consuming more than 3500W.
data_description.power_limit_hysteresis_w: How many Watts consumption must drop below the maximum threshold before the AC can turn back on. Example: threshold 3500W, hysteresis 800W → turns on only when consumption drops below 2700W. Avoids rapid on/off cycles.
data_description.power_limit_restore_min: How many minutes consumption must stay below the restart threshold before the AC turns back on. Example: 5 minutes → if consumption drops but rises again within 5 minutes, AC does not restart.
data_description.power_limit_notify_tts: If enabled: Google Home announces when the AC is turned off or on due to power protection.
data_description.power_limit_notify_telegram: If enabled: Telegram alerts when the AC is turned off or on due to power protection.

emergenza_simple.title: Heat emergency
emergenza_simple.description: Configure the 'Heat emergency' switch behavior. When manually activated, the thermostat completely ignores solar production and turns on the AC based only on temperature, like simple mode. It auto-deactivates 5 minutes before night mode or when temperature returns to normal.

data.emergency_heat_threshold: Temperature above target to turn on in emergency (°C)
data.emergency_heat_end_threshold: Temperature above target to consider emergency over (°C)

data_description.emergency_heat_active: Activate or deactivate the heat emergency switch directly from here. When active the thermostat completely ignores solar production and turns on the AC based only on temperature. Deactivates automatically 5 minutes before night mode or when temperature returns within the configured threshold.
data_description.emergency_heat_threshold: How many degrees above target to turn on in emergency mode. Example: 1.5°C with target 25°C → turns on from 26.5°C ignoring solar.
data_description.emergency_heat_end_threshold: When temperature drops within this margin of target, emergency is considered over and switch deactivates automatically. Example: 0.7°C with target 25°C → emergency ends when it drops below 25.7°C.
